title: Overdraft race in withdrawals
root_cause: Time-of-check-to-time-of-use race: withdraw() did SELECT balance then UPDATE balance in READ COMMITTED without locking the row, so N concurrent withdrawals could all read the same pre-withdrawal balance, all pass the `balance >= amount` check, and all debit — driving no-overdraft accounts negative.
fix: Added FOR UPDATE row lock to the balance SELECT in withdraw(), so concurrent withdrawals on the same account serialize on the row lock; check-and-debit becomes atomic while unrelated accounts remain independent.

repro_report.example_violation: overdraft violated: 10/10 withdrawals succeeded, final balance -1000 < 0 (initial 1000)

checks.name: same_behaviour
checks.detail: 40 sequential requests matched the original exactly

checks.name: agent_reproduction_test
checks.detail: the agent's own reproduction test passed 3/3 runs

repro_code:
import threading

def reproduce(connect, service) -> str | None:
    # Setup: set account 1 to known balance 1000
    with connect() as conn:
        conn.execute("UPDATE accounts SET balance = 1000 WHERE id = 1")

    n = 10
    amount = 200  # total 2000 > 1000, each single withdraw should succeed alone
    barrier = threading.Barrier(n)
    errors = []
    results = [None]*n

    def worker(idx):
        try:
            with connect() as conn:
                barrier.wait(timeout=10)
                try:
                    service.withdraw(conn, 1, amount)
                    results[idx] = "ok"
                except Exception as e:
                    # Expected: InsufficientFunds or ValueError etc.
                    # Record as rejected; unexpected exceptions also counted as rejected
                    # but to avoid false positives, treat any exception as rejected
                    results[idx] = f"rejected:{type(e).__name__}"
        except Exception as e:
            results[idx] = f"error:{type(e).__name__}"

    threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(i,)) for i in range(n)]
    for t in threads:
        t.start()
    for t in threads:
        t.join(timeout=20)

    ok = sum(1 for r in results if r == "ok")
    # Check final balance
    with connect() as conn:
        row = conn.execute("SELECT balance FROM accounts WHERE id = 1").fetchone()
        final = row[0] if row else None

    # Money rule: account without overdraft must never go negative,
    # and total withdrawn cannot exceed initial 1000.
    # Buggy code lets all 10 succeed -> final = -1000
    if final is not None and final < 0:
        return f"overdraft violated: {ok}/10 withdrawals succeeded, final balance {final} < 0 (initial 1000)"
    if ok * amount > 1000:
        return f"overdraft violated: withdrew {ok*amount} from 1000 (final {final})"
    return None
